Hi Priya — thank you for the data, that's really helpful. Quick read: the March->April jump aligns with the new triage route and a higher embedding churn for follow-ups. Two immediate paths:

- Short-term: provision a +30% burst corridor on your Dedicated pool and enable prefix KV caching on the triage flow. That reduces redundant token counts for retries and multi-turn sessions.
- Medium-term: a license shift to a higher commit with monthly true-up gives you predictable throughput and discounts on token unit price. We can craft a 3-month ramp (commit step-up) so you don't front-load budget.

I'll pull cost delta numbers and a proposed mutual action plan for sign-off. Ben, Laura — can you review the perf PDF and suggest tangible econ levers?

Can we do a 30-min sync Thursday 11am PT?

—Marcus

Thanks Marcus. Quick notes after skimming the CSV and perf PDF:
- April token mix shows 62% generation tokens, 28% embeddings, 10% control/meta. If Nexa moves ~20% of non-critical embedding lookups to weekly batch jobs (cached index snapshots), that alone reduces monthly embedding units by ~15–18%.
- Pricing options: a stepped commit (3mo ramp) reduces unit costs by ~12% at the first tier and ~20% after sustained commit. We can include a short burst credit in the first month of the new commit to cover the April overshoot.

I'll prepare a short cost delta table for the Thursday sync and include a redline of options (commit sizes, burst credit, SLA margin).

Ben

Hi all — some quick technical levers from the infra side:
- Enable continuous batching with a 40ms latency budget for low-priority triage calls; this typically cuts per-token latency costs by ~8–12% without user-visible degradation.
- Deploy a quantized model variant for the background scoring path (reduces GPU compute cost by ~30% for that route).
- Short-term KV caching TTL tweak: increase to 90s for session tokens that are read-heavy.

I'll attach a proposed rollout plan in the MAP. Marcus — Ben: I left notes in the perf PDF about observed p95 spikes and the likely root cause (concurrent cold KV misses).
